deep.reconstruction:
PART A (French note). Gauss copies a sentence from Legendre, 'Recherches d'analyse indéterminée', Mém. Acad. Paris 1785, p. 520 (or 820; see corrections): 'In this demonstration we have only supposed that there is a prime b of the form 4n-1 which can divide the formula xx+Ayy.' He comments, signed G.: 'It would have been better to have proved this, or not to claim to have given a demonstration in which the most essential part is missing.' This is Legendre's attempted proof of quadratic reciprocity. One case needs an auxiliary prime b ≡ 3 (mod 4) with -A (or A, depending on sign convention) a quadratic residue mod b, i.e. b dividing some xx+Ayy with x, y coprime. Legendre did not prove such a b exists. Elsewhere he also relied on primes in arithmetic progressions, which was likewise unproved. Gauss makes the same objection in print in Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), arts. 151 and 296-297.

PART B (German, ternary/orthogonality lemma). The struck heading is illegible. Setting: integer vectors x=(m,n,p) and y=(μ,ν,π) with x·y = mμ+nν+pπ = 0. Put C = m²+n²+p² and Γ = μ²+ν²+π².

Identity 1: C(μ²+ν²) = (mν-nμ)² + Γp².
Identity 2 (symmetric): Γ(m²+n²) = (mν-nμ)² + Cπ².

Proof (mine). The two-square identity gives (m²+n²)(μ²+ν²) = (mμ+nν)² + (mν-nμ)². Orthogonality gives mμ+nν = -pπ, so (m²+n²)(μ²+ν²) = p²π² + (mν-nμ)². Adding p²(μ²+ν²) to both sides gives C(μ²+ν²) = (mν-nμ)² + p²Γ. Identity 2 follows the same way. As polynomial identities, each left side minus right side equals (mμ+nν-pπ)(mμ+nν+pπ).

Consequence (implicit). Write a = mν-nμ. Then a² ≡ -Γp² (mod C) and a² ≡ -Cπ² (mod Γ). So when p is prime to C, a/p is a square root of -Γ mod C. This is the link Gauss exploits in DA arts. 278-292: the lattice orthogonal to a vector of norm C carries a binary form of determinant C, and Γ is represented by it.

Statement I: if x and x'=(m',n',p') have the same norm C and are both orthogonal to y, then Γ (Gauss later adds 'or C') is composite. Sketch: by Identity 2, a and a' = m'ν-n'μ both satisfy a² ≡ a'² ≡ -Cπ² (mod Γ). So Γ divides (a-a')(a+a'), which gives a factor of Γ unless a ≡ ±a' (mod Γ).

Statement II: if x is orthogonal to two vectors y and y' (implicitly of the same norm Γ), then Γ or C or both are composite. Here a/p and a'/p (a' = mν'-nμ') are both square roots of -Γ mod C. Hence (a/p) ± (a'/p) is divisible by C when C is prime ('theilb. d. C' = theilbar durch C). That forces the two representations to coincide essentially. Otherwise gcd(a±a', C) splits C.

This is a Euler-type 'two representations give a factorization' principle, transferred from sums of two squares to orthogonal pairs of sums of three squares. The next step, showing the representations then coincide, is not written out.
errors: Statements I and II are stated without the necessary qualification 'essentially different' (not obtained by sign changes, coordinate reflections or automorphs). As literally written they are false.
Counterexample to I: y=(1,1,0) with Γ=2 prime; x=(1,-1,1) and x'=(1,-1,-1), both of norm C=3 prime, both orthogonal to y, with x' ≠ ±x.
A Γ=1 case also breaks I: y=(0,0,1), x=(1,2,0), x'=(2,1,0) with C=5 prime. Here Γ=1 is neither prime nor composite.
Counterexample to II (after permuting coordinates so the third entry is nonzero): x=(1,0,1) with C=2; y=(1,1,-1) and y'=(1,-1,-1), both of norm Γ=3 prime and both orthogonal to x.
In II the division by p presupposes p ≠ 0 and gcd(p,C)=1. Read as a congruence mod C, the conclusion 'divisible by C' is correct when C is prime.

results.what: Critique of Legendre's 1785 proof of quadratic reciprocity for assuming, without proof, an auxiliary prime b ≡ 3 mod 4 dividing xx+Ayy
results.modern_name: Gap in Legendre's proof of quadratic reciprocity (existence of auxiliary primes)

results.what: C(μ²+ν²) = (mν-nμ)² + Γp² and Γ(m²+n²) = (mν-nμ)² + Cπ² for orthogonal integer vectors
results.modern_name: Lagrange/Brahmagupta two-square identity applied to orthogonal vectors; norm of the orthogonal-complement lattice
results.usually_credited_to: Euler/Lagrange (identity); Gauss DA arts. 278-292 (ternary forms and sums of three squares)

results.what: Two essentially distinct orthogonal configurations with the same norms force C or Γ to be composite; (a ± a')/p ≡ 0 mod C
results.modern_name: Uniqueness of representations by binary forms of prime determinant; Euler-type factorization from two representations

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's objection to Legendre's auxiliary-prime assumption is famous from DA art. 297, so this is just an early private version. The three-square orthogonality identities are elementary preparatory material for his known theory of ternary forms. The informal composite-ness criteria are routine and incompletely qualified.

checkable.asserts: Identity 1 holds modulo the orthogonality relation m*mu+n*nu+p*pi=0
Counterexample to Statement I as literally stated: two distinct vectors of prime norm 3 orthogonal to a vector of prime norm 2

Instance of a² ≡ -Γp² mod C: x=(1,3,2) with C=14 and y=(3,-1,0); with the substitution, a=3*(-3)-1*2=-11 and Γ=13, so 121+52=173, which is not 0 mod 14. This instance does not satisfy the stated check and needs replacing; the general congruence follows from Identity 1, since C(μ²+ν²) ≡ 0 mod C.

transcription_corrections: 'Theilb. d. C' should be read as 'theilbar durch C' (divisible by C), not 'divisor of C'. The meaning is that (mν-nμ)/p ± (mν'-nμ')/p ≡ 0 mod C.
The page reference may read 'p. 820' in the image. Legendre's memoir occupies roughly pp. 465-559 of the 1785 volume, so 'p. 520' is the plausible reading.
Struck heading at top of Part B ('Lex dem Lemma') is illegible; it is possibly 'Zu dem Lemma' or similar.
In Statement I the right-hand side is mm+nn+pp = m'm'+n'n'+p'p' (the first term was struck and rewritten). Above Γ is the insertion 'oder C', and the word below is 'zusammengesetzt'.
In Statement II the second vector is (μ',ν',π') with the same (m,n,p): mμ'+nν'+pπ'=0.
